correctness.rationale: For each strictly positive unit- or double-unit good, greedy discrepancy belongs to {0,1,2}; the only rounds where a competing allocation has lower absolute discrepancy (greedy 2 vs competitor 0) are paired injectively with an immediately preceding round having opposite cost difference +2. Every prefix therefore has no smaller cumulative envy. Explicit four-good allocations and lower bounds give exact boundary costs 6 vs 5, 6 vs 4, and 5 vs 3; finite exhaustive checker verifies all bounded counts and three-agent minimality. The proof excludes zero-valued arrivals and arbitrary two-level ratios.

value.rationale: This finds a nontrivial, all-horizons exact online greedy island for two equal-valued agents in the new fixed-order cumulative maximum envy objective, between the previously known {0,1} trivial per-round bound and general fixed-order hardness. It establishes three sharp four-item failure boundaries that isolate item indivisibility, population size, and zero-valued waiting rounds; the positive theorem is infinite, not a finite census.
